questions.q: How many pairs of letters are there in the word 'COMPUTER' each of which has as many letters between them (in the word) as there are between them in the English alphabet?
questions.solution: Check pairs by absolute alphabet difference equalling their word-position difference. Matching pairs are M–R, U–T, U–R and T–R, giving four.

questions.q: Four of the following five letter-pairs are alike in a certain way based on their positions in the English alphabet, and hence form a group. Find the one that does NOT belong to the group.
questions.solution: NQ,SV,CF,HK each advance three positions. LP advances four and is different.

questions.q: In four of the following five number pairs, the second number is obtained by multiplying the first number with one less than itself (for example, 5 → 5×4 = 20). Find the pair that does NOT fit this pattern.
questions.solution: Each second number should equal n(n−1). For 9 this is 72 rather than 81.

questions.q: Statements: All lamps are bulbs. No bulb is a switch. Some switches are wires. Conclusions: I. No lamp is a switch. II. Some switches are not lamps. Which of the conclusions logically follow(s)?
questions.solution: Every lamp is a bulb, and no bulb is a switch. Thus no lamp is a switch. Existing switches from the third statement cannot be lamps either.

questions.solution: The chain W>X≥Y>Z≥V gives W>V and X>Z. Both follow.

questions.q: Statements: Some doctors are teachers. All teachers are readers. No reader is a painter. Conclusions: I. No teacher is a painter. II. Some painters are not doctors. Which of the conclusions logically follow(s)?
questions.solution: Teachers are readers and cannot be painters, so I follows. The statements do not establish that any painter exists or is outside doctors.
